first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation, with prior evidence of durable adoption gains. Promotional pricing is the most salient alternative given competitor pricing, but its reported 30-day retention harm conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; verify both the preferred intervention and that downside before committing.

final.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-simplification experiment only for simple-workspace self-serve accounts, explicitly excluding complex-workspace accounts. This directly addresses declining onboarding completion and activation while aligning with sustainable qualified revenue. The verified evidence shows substantial completion and time-to-value gains, but also a 9% churn increase when complex accounts lose necessary setup steps. Promotional pricing is rejected because its verified 12% retention decline undermines long-term value. Measure completion, activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and 60-day retention before considering expansion.
